hints: At the greatest height, the vertical velocity of the particle is instantaneously zero ($v = 0$).
Use the vertical motion formula $v = u - gt$ with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and time $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Substitute $0 = u - 10(3)$ and solve for initial speed $u$.
walkthrough:
At the maximum height, vertical velocity is zero ($v = 0$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$):
$$v = u - gt$$
$$0 = u - 10(3)$$
$$u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the kinematic variables for vertical motion under gravity (taking upwards as positive):
- Initial velocity: $+u$
- Acceleration: $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$
- Time to reach highest point: $t = 3\text{ s}$
- Velocity at highest point: $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$

Apply the constant-acceleration equation:
$$v = u + at$$
$$0 = u + (-10)(3)$$
$$0 = u - 30$$
Add $30$ to both sides:
$$u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the initial projection speed of the particle is $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Use the kinematic equation $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$ relating speeds and vertical displacement.
Substitute $v = 0$, $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Solve $0 = 30^2 - 2(10)s$ to determine the maximum height $s$.
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall the equation relating displacement to initial and final velocities under gravity:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
Taking upwards as positive:
- $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$
- $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the peak
- $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$

Substitute into the formula:
$$0^2 = 30^2 + 2(-10)s$$
$$0 = 900 - 20s$$
Add $20s$ to both sides:
$$20s = 900$$
Divide by $20$:
$$s = \frac{900}{20} = 45\text{ m}$$
Thus, the greatest height reached by the particle above the ground is $45\text{ m}$.
